late: This synthetic handbook section describes how late work is handled in the teaching programme. Late submission is normally penalized. The penalty is ten percent of the available marks for each calendar day after the deadline, and work that is more than five days late receives no marks. Dr. Saeed Anwar coordinates the assessment office and publishes the final penalty table every semester. Students who miss a deadline for personal reasons should contact the coordinator as early as possible. Illness extensions require medical evidence before the deadline. The evidence must be a signed note from a licensed doctor that states the dates of the illness. Extensions for non-medical reasons need written approval from the course coordinator and are granted only in rare cases. An older version of this handbook allowed students to send medical evidence up to seven days after the deadline, but that rule was withdrawn and must not be used. Group assignments follow the same rules, and one extension request covers the whole group when every member is affected. Requests sent after marking has started cannot be accepted. All decisions are recorded in the student portal so that the history of each request can be checked later.
password: This synthetic IT help section explains account access for students and staff. Reset a forgotten password using the recovery link. The link is shown below the login box on the sign-in page and is sent to the registered university email address. It stays valid for thirty minutes, and a new request cancels any earlier link. Never share recovery codes. The help desk will never ask for a password or a recovery code by phone, chat or email. If the registered email address is no longer available, the user must visit the IT desk with a student card so that the identity can be checked in person. Staff accounts are reset by the IT desk only, because they give access to grades and personal records. After three wrong password attempts the account is locked for fifteen minutes to protect it from guessing. Passwords should contain at least twelve characters and should not be reused on other websites. Students are encouraged to enable the second step sign-in option in their profile settings, which adds a code from a phone application to every new login.
assignment: This synthetic assessment section explains how coursework is delivered. Upload assignments through the learning portal. Submit the final file as a PDF. Files in other formats are not opened by the markers, and a document that cannot be opened is treated as not submitted. The portal accepts files up to twenty megabytes, so large figures should be compressed before the upload, and the student must keep a copy of the confirmation message that appears after every successful upload because the confirmation is the only proof of submission that the office accepts during a dispute. Group projects are uploaded by the team leader only, and every team member must be named on the first page of the document. Laboratory reports for practical sessions are different because they are handed to the instructor on paper at the start of the next session and are not accepted through the portal. Handwritten work must be scanned clearly before it is uploaded, and photographs taken at an angle may be rejected by the coordinator. Submissions are accepted until midnight on the deadline day according to the portal clock, and a resubmission before the deadline replaces the earlier file without any penalty.
contractor: This synthetic workplace policy describes remote work rules for different groups of people. Employees may work remotely for up to two days each week when the line manager approves the plan in advance. Contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract permits it. Employee rules do not apply to contractors. A contractor whose contract is silent on remote work must work on site until the contract is amended by the human resources office. Visitors and interns follow a separate internship policy and should not use this section. Remote work from another country is not allowed for any group without written approval from the legal office, because tax and data protection rules differ between countries. Everyone who works remotely must use the company virtual private network and must keep work devices locked when they are not in use. Managers review remote work plans every quarter, and a plan can be withdrawn with one week of notice when the needs of the team change. Equipment such as laptops remains the property of the company and must be returned at the end of the arrangement.
printer: This synthetic equipment guide collects short troubleshooting notes for office devices. For blank printer pages, check ink levels and run the cleaning utility. Print a test page afterwards. If the test page is still blank, open the printer menu and make sure that the correct paper size is selected, because a wrong size can cause empty output. Warning: switch the device off and wait ten minutes before touching any internal part, since the heating unit stays hot. For a blank scanner image, check document placement and select the correct scanning source. A scanner glass with fingerprints can also lower quality, so clean it with a soft dry cloth. A printer that makes noise but pulls no paper usually has a dirty roller, and the roller can be wiped with a slightly damp cloth after unplugging the cable. Streaks across the page point to a clogged print head, and a second cleaning cycle is usually enough. Each device model has its own manual, and the instructions for one model must not be applied to another model without checking. Replace cartridges only with the type listed in the manual.
